name: Apricot Chicken Sheet Pan Dinner Recipe + VIDEO

ingredients.buy: 2 lb (about 12 large carrots), peeled and thinly sliced

writer_notes: All 14 bought ingredients are used by a step; no step uses anything not on the buy list. Glaze step (6) consumes apricot jam, soy sauce, Worcestershire, cider vinegar, and cornstarch; step 2 consumes all five dry spices.
Source step 5 has a transcription typo ('potatoes are vegetables are cooked through'); rendered correctly as 'vegetables are tender' in head.steps and make_it.
At 14 servings the food exceeds one sheet pan; method and step 1 instruct using two or three pans so nothing steams. Flag for card reviewer if a single-pan image is used.
Only dollar figure in prose is the ${{cost_ps}} token plus the $1/month membership line; no per-line costs used.

shop_smart claims trace to locked buy strings only: 'one jar covers the batch' vs '3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp' jam; 'family pack' vs '6 1/4 lb (about 14 breasts)'; carrots '2 lb' and potatoes '3 1/2 lb' verbatim. No per-ounce or lasts-several-batches claim made (no cost_lines in dispatch to prove such).

prose.intro_html:
Here is a weeknight truth worth banking: the sheet pan is the most honest appliance in your kitchen. One pan, one temperature, and dinner that does not ask you to hover. This apricot chicken lays boneless skinless chicken breast, creamer potatoes, and sliced carrots on the same tray, then finishes with a sweet and savory apricot glaze you stir together while the oven does the heavy lifting.

The numbers hold up too. Every serving lands at 470 calories with 48.9 grams of protein, so you get a full, satisfying plate that still fits inside a real meal-prep budget. That is the whole game here: real food, real protein, and a cleanup that fits in the trash bag your parchment came out of.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the chicken in a family pack. The recipe wants 6 1/4 pounds of boneless skinless breast, which is roughly 14 breasts, so grab the largest pack the case offers instead of the little foam trays. One big pack, one price, done.

Grab a single 2 pound bag of carrots and about 3 1/2 pounds of small creamer potatoes. Creamer or baby potatoes save you the peeling, and halved they roast in the same window as the carrots, so nothing on the pan finishes early or late.

The apricot jam is the only specialty item, and one standard jar covers this whole batch with room to spare, since the glaze only asks for 3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons. Soy sauce, Worcestershire, cider vinegar, cornstarch, and the five dry spices are pantry regulars, so if your shelf is stocked you are buying produce and chicken and calling it a day.
prose.make_it:
Heat the oven to 375 degrees F and line your rimmed baking sheets with parchment. At 14 servings this is more than one pan of food, so use two or three sheets and give everything room. Crowd the pan and you steam instead of roast, and nobody wants a soggy potato.

Scatter the halved potatoes and sliced carrots across the pans. In a small bowl, stir together the salt, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika, and onion powder so your seasoning is one even blend and not five separate sprinkles.

Drizzle the vegetables with half of the oil, dust them with half of the seasoning, and toss until every piece is coated. Push them to the edges to open up the center. Lay the chicken breasts in that middle lane, drizzle with the rest of the oil, and hit them with the remaining seasoning.

Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the chicken reads 165 degrees F on a thermometer. While that runs, whisk the apricot jam, soy sauce, Worcestershire, cider vinegar, and cornstarch in a bowl and microwave it in 30 second bursts, stirring between each, until it thickens slightly. About a minute total does it. When the pan comes out, brush that glaze over the chicken and serve.
prose.portion_html:
Here is the method that keeps 14 containers honest: weigh, do not eyeball. Set your empty container on the scale and zero it, then weigh the full cooked pan of chicken, potatoes, and carrots. Divide that total by 14 and portion to that gram number, container after container.

The easy version is one chicken breast per box, since the buy works out to about 14 breasts, plus an even scoop of potatoes and carrots and a brush of the apricot glaze over the top. Weighing the first two or three containers trains your eye, and the last one comes out the same size as the first instead of the sad, half-empty box nobody wants to grab on Thursday.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Let us talk money, because that is the reason we cook in batches. This one comes in at ${{cost_ps}} a serving, and for that you get 470 calories and 48.9 grams of protein on a plate with a real vegetable and a real carbohydrate. Try pricing a glazed chicken plate with potatoes at a counter and see how fast you clear ten dollars.

The math is simple. Cook 14 of these on a Sunday and you have lunches and dinners handled for less than the cost of one delivery order with the fees stacked on. The savings are not a coupon, they are a habit.

And if you are reading this without a membership, that is a dollar a month to unlock the full board and every recipe on it. One dollar. Your future self, staring into the fridge on a Wednesday night with dinner already made, will thank you.
prose.upsell_html: Roast it once, eat it all week. That is the sheet pan promise, and this apricot chicken keeps it with sweet glaze, tender vegetables, and protein that actually fills you up. Build it into your rotation, and when you want the next one already portioned and priced out, the whole board is waiting for a dollar a month.

head.description: Apricot chicken sheet pan dinner scaled to 14 meal-prep servings. Boneless skinless chicken breast, creamer potatoes, and carrots roast on one pan with a sweet-savory apricot glaze. 470 calories and 48.9 g protein per serving.
head.keywords: apricot chicken sheet pan, sheet pan chicken dinner, meal prep chicken, high protein meal prep, budget chicken dinner, apricot glaze chicken, chicken and potatoes sheet pan
steps: Heat the oven to 375 degrees F and line large rimmed baking sheets with parchment paper. At 14 servings use two or three pans. Scatter the halved potatoes and sliced carrots across the sheets.
In a small bowl, stir together the salt, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika, and onion powder into one even seasoning blend.
Drizzle the vegetables with half of the oil and half of the seasoning. Toss until coated, then push them to the edges of the pans to make room in the center.
Place the chicken breasts in the center of the pans. Drizzle with the remaining oil and sprinkle with the remaining seasoning.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the chicken reaches 165 degrees F internally.

Meanwhile, whisk the apricot jam, soy sauce, Worcestershire sauce, cider vinegar, and cornstarch in a medium bowl. Microwave on high in 30 second intervals, stirring between each, until slightly thickened, about 1 minute total.
Once the chicken and vegetables are done, brush the apricot glaze over the chicken and serve.
